whole-add.title: Adding whole numbers
whole-add.method: Read each number by place value. Add the ones, then the tens and any remaining places. When a column totals ten or more, exchange ten units for one unit in the next place. Record the carried amount before continuing. In a horizontal problem, you may rewrite the numbers vertically; the ones must still line up.
whole-add.mistake: A carried ten belongs in the next column. Do not write a two-digit total into a single place or forget to include a carry in the next sum.
whole-add.check: Subtract one addend from the sum. The result should equal the other addend.

whole-sub.title: Subtracting whole numbers
whole-sub.method: Start in the ones place and subtract corresponding places. If a top digit is too small, exchange one unit from the next place for ten units in the current place. Mark both changes: the giving place decreases by one and the receiving place increases by ten. Continue left, using the changed digits.
whole-sub.mistake: Do not reverse the digits just because the lower digit is larger. Subtraction keeps its original order. When a zero is involved, follow the exchange across the places rather than changing every zero independently.
whole-sub.check: Add the difference to the number subtracted. You should recover the starting number.

whole-mul.title: Multiplying whole numbers
whole-mul.method: Use known multiplication facts and place value together. Multiply the top number by each digit of the lower number, starting with the ones. Regroup when a product exceeds nine. If the lower number has more than one digit, write a separate partial product for each place and add the partial products. A tens digit represents tens, not ones.
whole-mul.mistake: A partial product for the tens place must be shifted one place. Keep a carried amount separate from the next multiplication fact, then add it once.
whole-mul.check: Estimate using nearby convenient numbers. You can also divide the product by one factor to recover the other.

whole-div.title: Dividing whole numbers
whole-div.method: Decide how many complete groups of the divisor fit into the current amount. Write a quotient digit, multiply it by the divisor, and subtract. Bring down the next digit and repeat. A zero quotient digit may be needed to hold a place. At the end, the remainder must be smaller than the divisor.
whole-div.mistake: Do not stop just because a current digit is smaller than the divisor. Check whether more digits remain to be brought down. A remainder equal to or larger than the divisor means another complete group fits.
whole-div.check: Multiply the quotient by the divisor and add the remainder. This must equal the dividend.

decimal-add.title: Adding decimals
decimal-add.method: Line up decimal points so that ones, tenths, and hundredths match. Add trailing zeros if they help you see the places; this does not change a number. Add from the smallest place shown and regroup as needed. Put the decimal point in the sum directly below the other decimal points.
decimal-add.mistake: Align decimal points, not the right-hand ends of the numbers. For example, a tenth must not be added to a hundredth merely because both digits happen to be last.
decimal-add.check: Subtract either addend from the sum. Estimate with nearby whole numbers to check the size of the answer.

decimal-sub.title: Subtracting decimals
decimal-sub.method: Align the decimal points and write equivalent trailing zeros when needed. Subtract from the smallest place. An exchange from one place gives ten units of the place immediately to its right, just as in whole-number subtraction. Keep the decimal point aligned in the difference.
decimal-sub.mistake: Adding a zero at the end of a decimal is allowed; moving its decimal point is not. Remember to reduce the place from which you exchanged one unit.
decimal-sub.check: Add the difference to the amount subtracted. Compare the total with the original decimal.

decimal-mul.title: Multiplying decimals
decimal-mul.method: First multiply using the digits as whole numbers. Count the decimal places in both original factors. Their total tells you where to place the decimal point in the product. Include leading zeros after the decimal point when needed, then remove unnecessary trailing zeros only when the value stays unchanged.
decimal-mul.mistake: Do not align decimal points as you would for addition. Multiplying by a positive number less than one makes a positive quantity smaller, so a large answer may indicate a misplaced point.
decimal-mul.check: Estimate the product before calculating. Divide the product by a nonzero factor to check the other factor.

decimal-div.title: Dividing decimals
decimal-div.method: If the divisor has decimal places, multiply both numbers by the same power of ten until the divisor is a whole number. The quotient stays the same. Divide using place value, keeping track of the decimal point in the quotient. These worksheets use the answers supplied by the existing calculation bank; do not round unless a question explicitly asks you to.
decimal-div.mistake: Moving only the divisor’s decimal point changes the problem. Apply the same shift to the dividend, and keep any zero needed to hold a quotient place.
decimal-div.check: Multiply the quotient by the original divisor. The result should return the original dividend.

fraction-add.title: Adding fractions
fraction-add.method: Fractions must refer to equal-sized parts before you combine them. For like denominators, add the numerators and keep the denominator. For unlike denominators, rewrite both fractions using a common denominator, then add. Convert a mixed number to an equivalent improper fraction when that makes the calculation easier. Finally, simplify the result.
fraction-add.mistake: Do not add the denominators. Rewriting a fraction requires multiplying its numerator and denominator by the same number. Our answer key shows an improper fraction beside its equivalent mixed number when the result is greater than one.
fraction-add.check: Subtract one original fraction from the total. Use equivalent fractions if necessary to compare the result with the other addend.

fraction-sub.title: Subtracting fractions
fraction-sub.method: Use a common denominator so both fractions name the same-sized parts. Subtract the numerators in the stated order and keep that common denominator. With mixed numbers, you can first convert to improper fractions. Simplify the difference; if it is greater than one, read the equivalent improper and mixed forms together.
fraction-sub.mistake: Keep the subtraction order. Subtracting denominators or changing only a numerator does not preserve the original quantities.
fraction-sub.check: Add the difference to the fraction subtracted. Simplify or find a common denominator to compare it with the starting amount.

fraction-mul.title: Multiplying fractions
fraction-mul.method: Write whole numbers over one and convert mixed numbers to improper fractions. Multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators. You may cancel common factors between a numerator and a denominator before multiplying, or simplify the product afterward. A common denominator is not required for multiplication.
fraction-mul.mistake: Do not multiply a mixed number’s whole part and fractional part separately and join them. Convert the entire mixed number first. Cancellation removes common factors, not digits that merely look alike.
fraction-mul.check: Estimate the size of each factor. A positive factor below one reduces the other positive factor. Check by dividing by a nonzero original factor.

fraction-div.title: Dividing fractions
fraction-div.method: Convert any mixed numbers to improper fractions and write whole numbers over one. Keep the first fraction, replace division with multiplication, and use the reciprocal of the second fraction. Multiply and simplify. The reciprocal is applied to the divisor only.
fraction-div.mistake: Do not flip the first fraction or both fractions. Division by a fraction below one can produce an answer larger than the dividend; this is consistent with asking how many smaller groups fit.
fraction-div.check: Multiply the quotient by the original divisor, not its reciprocal. The result should equal the dividend.

round.title: Rounding decimals
round.method: Identify the requested place first. Look one place to its right: a digit from zero to four keeps the target digit, while five to nine increases it by one. Remove the digits beyond the requested place after completing any carry. A whole-number answer and an answer to the nearest tenth use different target places.
round.mistake: Do not round an intermediate digit first. Read the requested place in each question rather than applying the same place to the whole sheet.
round.check: Locate the two neighboring whole numbers or tenths. The rounded value should be the nearer neighbor; an exact midpoint rounds upward for these positive-number examples.
